analysis: Scope: SSD checkpoint concurrency changes (T-041, TB-007, A-001). SSDCheckpointFileCoordinator.swift head 65-220 replaces the single-owner FIFO queue with per-path shared/exclusive leases. Traced the lease state machine: admits() (119-124) grants exclusive only with no holders and grants shared only when no exclusive holder; enqueue (144-159) grants immediately only if no waiters, which preserves FIFO and stops writer starvation; its defer is registered only after the idle guard, so no empty FileLeases entry is left behind; store() (140-142) drops empty entries, so tryAcquire (83-91) does not wedge. cancel (161-182) re-admits waiters after a queued exclusive request is withdrawn. release (184-197) locates the holder by identity. tryUpgrade (199-208) requires a sole active shared holder and no waiters. downgrade (210-220) admits queued shared requests. All of these transitions run under the lock, and continuations resume outside it. I found no lock-state inconsistency that would let a writer, scan or retirement overlap a reader. Read.swift head 128-129 and 204 now take shared leases for stage reads, including the retry handoff. Maintenance.swift head 29-39 only threads an optional unusedSince value into SSDOwnedEntryRetirement.remove; that implementation is not supplied. Readers now block exclusive maintenance, and tryAcquire skips files with readers. This is bounded by stage budgets, and TTL lookup uses index time. No crypto, HMAC naming, AAD, TTL constant or scope-salt logic changed. Open integration questions: (1) readAttempt is not visible. Any mutation it performs under the lease must now use tryUpgrade, or it can disturb a concurrent same-file reader. Examples are sliding-TTL touch, removeCorrupt after an auth failure, and forgetMissing. Whether readers re-validate the index and epoch after acquire also needs checking. (2) The unusedSince semantics in SSDOwnedEntryRetirement.remove need checking. Callers' retirement must not skip expired or revoked entries. A file should be retired only once it has gone unused since the given time. (3) The write and duplicate-validation paths should still request exclusive leases, which is the makeAccess default.
